Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & quantization trade study for FinWave

Hi Laura / Michael —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

- Objective: validate model fit for your RAG/assistant workflows and quantify latency/throughput improvements from quantization without unacceptable quality regressions.
- Hypothesis: AWQ/GPTQ quantization (4-bit/8-bit variants) and FP8 paths can materially improve throughput on our Dedicated pool; trade-offs in generation quality depend heavily on prompt shape and evals.

Recommended immediate steps we discussed:
1) Run the FinWave prompt set (attached: finwave_prompt_set_v2.json) across 3 config buckets: AWQ (q4_0/q4_K variants), GPTQ (q8/q4 variants), and FP8 inference builds.
2) Metrics to measure: token-level throughput, p50/p95 latency, memory footprint, and quality delta vs baseline (perplexity + human-rated score on representative prompt subsets).
3) We will provide a bench summary and recommended model/config (likely a 13B- or 30B-class open model variant) plus a rollout plan (canary + fallback to float model).

Attachments: quant-tradeoffs-AWQ-vs-GPTQ.xlsx (trade table), bench_summary_20270226.md, finwave_prompt_set_v2.json

Proposed timeline: quick pilot results by EOD Monday (02/29) if we can get confirmation on the prompt set and any priority personas; full evals and recommended config by Wed (03/03).

Next steps for you: please confirm the three priority personas/prompts we should prioritize and whether you need 99th percentile latency guarantees or just p95/p50.

Thanks —

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. That timeline works for us. A couple clarifications:

- Priority personas: (1) Account opening assistant, (2) Compliance Q&A (short-form recovery answers), (3) Transaction categorization prompts (batch).
- For SLAs: we care most about p95 for interactive flows (account opening, compliance Q&A). Batch jobs (categorization) can tolerate higher latency.
- Can you include expected throughput assumptions for our committed Dedicated pool (we plan to reserve 8x A100-equivalent GPUs)? Need to understand cost/throughput tradeoffs.

Also, please include any prompt engineering knobs you recommend for reducing hallucinations in the compliance flows.

Thanks —

Folks — forwarding the FinWave confirmation (below). They want p95 guarantees on interactive flows and will reserve an 8x A100-equivalent pool.

Ask: can we run the three config buckets on the finwave_prompt_set_v2.json and return a succinct bench summary with: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, VRAM usage, and a quick human-rated quality delta for the three persona prompt subsets? Please also include a short note on model-fit observations (e.g., system prompt sensitivity, common hallucination patterns).

Quick guidance based on prior trade studies:
- AWQ (4-bit) tends to give the best throughput uplift (2-3x) on our runtime but occasionally shows subtle generation artifacts on long-coherence prompts; tends to be safe on retrieval-augmented short prompts.
- GPTQ (8-bit / q4 variants) is a middle ground — decent throughput gains with lower quality delta in our prior benches.
- FP8 on supported kernels can provide good latency for some 30B models but requires careful kernel selection and may increase memory pressure in mixed workloads.

Please prioritize the compliance Q&A persona as their highest sensitivity.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks — quick plan below. I can run the pilot on our Dedicated test cluster (8x A100-equivalent emulation) and produce the bench_summary by EOD Monday assuming no blocking issues.

Pilot plan (high level):
- Workloads: compliance Q&A (interactive), account opening (multi-turn), batch categorization (throughput).
- Models/configs: baseline FP32/FP16, AWQ q4 variants on 13B/30B-class, GPTQ q8/q4 variants on 13B/30B-class, FP8 build for the chosen 30B where available.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, peak VRAM, end-to-end quality (auto metrics + 20 human-rated examples per persona).
- Quick findings (prelim local runs): AWQ-q4_0 on 13B: ~2.3x tokens/sec vs FP16, p95 reduced by 45% on short prompts, quality delta ~= -2 to -4% on human-rated compliance checks. GPTQ-q8 on 30B: ~1.6x tokens/sec, quality delta ~= -1 to -2%. FP8 (30B): latency similar to GPTQ, but memory footprint increased ~10% in our runtime due to kernel buffers; quality comparable to FP16 for retrieval prompts.

Resource ask: need access to FinWave example logs for the compliance persona (to ensure prompts match prod). Laura — can you drop a small sample (10 examples) into the Drive folder?

I'll attach full bench spreadsheet to the shared drive when ready.

-rishi
